title: The Carousel
lyrics:
The lights dim in a quiet, intimate room. Four stools sit in a half-circle. Harry Chapin, Stevie Nicks, Rodney Atkins, and Kenny Chesney sit with their acoustic guitars, looking directly at you. They aren't singing to a stadium tonight; they are singing to you, reflecting the reality of raising kids back to you.

Harry begins, picking a gentle, familiar melody on his guitar. His voice is earnest, carrying that familiar warning.

"You know, you blink, and the years just vanish into the ether. You promise yourself you'll slow down, that when the current project is done, you'll have the time. But the secret is, the time is right now. Don't wait until Wesley is grown, dealing with his own hassles and his own life, to realize you miss the noise. The sandbox is only there for a minute before it rusts."

Stevie steps to the microphone, the silver fringe on her shawl catching the low light. Her voice is hauntingly beautiful and grounded.

"I took my love, I took it down... You build this whole world, you build a foundation, but the seasons change faster than you can brace for them. When you and Michelle look at Ruby, you see how fast the reflection in the snow fades. Even children get older. Don't let the landslide of time break your heart—just hold onto their hands while you're still the one guiding them."

Rodney grins, breaking the melancholy with an upbeat, rhythmic strum, tapping his boot on the floor.

"It ain't just about the time slipping by, man, it's about what they're picking up while you aren't even looking. Wesley is watching every single move you make. He’s going to talk how you talk, walk how you walk, and learn how to treat people by watching how you are with Michelle. He wants to be just like you. That’s a heavy crown, but there's no better one to wear."

Kenny brings it home, adjusting his hat and slowing the tempo down to a quiet, reflective acoustic beat.

"You probably had all these wild plans and independence before you built this family. You thought you knew what your future looked like. But then you look up one day, watching Ruby grow into her own person, and you realize all those late nights, all the chaos, and all the loud mornings weren't keeping you from your life... there goes your life. Right there in front of you. And it's better than anything you had planned."

The four of them fall into a final, blended harmony, their voices echoing in the quiet room:

The cat's in the cradle, but the carousel keeps spinning,
They're watching you now, learning your every move.
Time makes you bolder, as the seasons keep changing,
Hold onto it all, because there goes your life.
